questions.stem: A teammate's `@RateLimit(perMinute = 60)` sits on `ApiController.search()`. `javap -v` on `ApiController.class` lists it, with `perMinute=60`, under `RuntimeInvisibleAnnotations`. At start-up the rate limiter calls `search.getAnnotation(RateLimit.class)`. What does it get?

options.text: `null`, since the attribute the annotation was written to is one reflection doesn't read
options.says: RuntimeInvisibleAnnotations holds CLASS-retained annotations: in the class file, values included, but never returned by reflection

options.text: `null`, since the compiler discarded the annotation before it wrote the class file
options.says: a discarded (SOURCE) annotation would not appear in javap's output at all; this one is in the class file

options.text: The annotation with `perMinute=60`, since it is in the class file the JVM loads
options.says: being in the class file is not enough: only RuntimeVisibleAnnotations reaches reflection

options.text: The annotation with `perMinute` at its default, since values of such annotations are not kept
options.says: the class file keeps the values (javap prints perMinute=60), and reflection returns nothing at all

origin.section: SOURCE Stops at the Compiler, CLASS Stops in the Class File, Only RUNTIME Reaches Reflection

questions.stem: Version 3.0 of an in-house metrics library changes `@Timed` from CLASS to RUNTIME. The checkout service upgrades to 3.0 and redeploys, but its `checkout-core` jar, whose classes carry `@Timed`, was built last month against 2.x and is not rebuilt. What does the metrics agent's `getAnnotation(Timed.class)` return on `checkout-core`'s methods?

options.text: `null` until `checkout-core` is rebuilt, since its class files still record `@Timed` as invisible
options.says: javac chose the attribute when it compiled checkout-core, from the retention Timed had then; the 3.0 release doesn't rewrite those class files

options.text: `null` until the agent is rebuilt, since its own class files still record `Timed` as CLASS
options.says: the reading side's compile doesn't matter; the annotated class's class file and Timed's current retention do

options.text: The annotation, since reflection decides visibility from the `Timed` class it loads at run time
options.says: reflection does check Timed's current retention, but only for annotations the class file holds as visible; these are recorded as invisible

options.text: The annotation, since the JVM moves the entry to the visible attribute when it loads `checkout-core`
options.says: the JVM never rewrites class files; the entry stays where javac put it

origin.section: javac Applies Retention When It Compiles the Annotated Class, and Reflection Checks It Again

questions.stem: The reporting service compiles against `audit-api.jar`, which declares `@AuditTrail` with RUNTIME retention, and marks the jar `provided`. The new application-server image doesn't supply it. At start-up a scanner calls `getDeclaredAnnotations()` on each service class and registers every class whose annotations include one named `AuditTrail`. What happens?

options.text: The service classes load and none is registered, since annotations whose type can't be loaded are left out of the result
options.says: reflection drops an annotation whose type it can't load, with no exception or warning; the classes load and run

options.text: The service classes load and all are registered, since the annotation is still in their class files
options.says: the entry is still in the class file, but reflection can't build an annotation of a type it can't load, so it returns none

options.text: Start-up fails with `NoClassDefFoundError` as the service classes load, since their class files refer to the missing type
options.says: the JVM loads a class without loading its annotation types; the classes load and their methods run

options.text: Start-up fails with `NoClassDefFoundError` as the scanner reads the annotations, since each must be resolved to be returned
options.says: reflection skips the unloadable annotation silently; NoClassDefFoundError comes only from code that names the missing type itself

origin.section: A RUNTIME Annotation Whose Class Is Missing at Run Time Disappears Without an Error

questions.stem: `@Fallback(to = LegacyPricing.class, attempts = 2)`, with RUNTIME retention, is on `PriceClient.quote()`. In the deployed image `Fallback.class` is present but `LegacyPricing.class` was removed. Code calls `getAnnotation(Fallback.class)` on `quote`, prints `attempts()`, then calls `to()`. What happens?

options.text: `getAnnotation` returns `null`, so `attempts()` is never reached, since a class the annotation names can't be loaded
options.says: the annotation's own type is present, so reflection returns it; only the missing element fails, and only when read

options.text: `getAnnotation` throws `TypeNotPresentException`, so `attempts()` is never reached, since the annotation can't be built
options.says: the annotation is built; the exception is deferred to the element that names the missing class

options.text: `attempts()` returns 2 and `to()` throws `TypeNotPresentException`, since only that element names the missing class
options.says: the page's run printed times=3 and then threw TypeNotPresentException from the Class-valued element; the AnnotatedElement javadoc specifies it

options.text: `attempts()` returns 2 and `to()` returns `null`, since an element naming a missing class is left unset
options.says: a Class-valued element whose class is missing throws TypeNotPresentException when read; it never returns null

origin.section: A RUNTIME Annotation Whose Class Is Missing at Run Time Disappears Without an Error
